study.title: DOSTA-Net: Domain-Shuffle Temporal Attention Network for Vessel Extraction in X-Ray Coronary Angiography Using Synthetic Data

imaging.modality_detail: X-ray coronary angiography (XCA) sequences; synthetic temporal XCA generated by DRR projection of L-system vessel trees fused with real contrast-free frames
imaging.frames_per_sequence: 3 input frames to model; synthetic test 7 frames, XCA30 4 frames, in-house reader set ~63 frames per sequence

public_dataset_used.detail: XCA30 public dataset (30 sequences) for external testing; DCA1 used to train nnU-Net/MT baselines

task.task_description: Annotation-free coronary artery extraction from XCA sequences by predicting contrast-free background (vessel layer via subtraction), trained on physics-informed synthetic temporal XCA plus unlabeled real sequences with domain-shuffle temporal attention and pseudo-label annealing loss; evaluated by vessel segmentation metrics and a radiologist reader study vs DSA and ETRPCA.
task.clinical_application: Vessel extraction for diagnosis and interventional treatment of coronary artery disease

temporal_evidence.quote: a temporal attention mechanism designed to enhance temporal consistency across frames in X-ray coronary angiography (XCA) sequences

method.explainability_method: Grad-CAM attention maps; t-SNE and MMD feature analysis

evaluation.external_validation_detail: Public real-world XCA30 dataset (30 sequences, out-of-distribution) for segmentation; in-house Northwestern 30-sequence set for blinded reader study

metrics.task: reader study vessel extraction quality (in-house set)

metrics.metric: MMD between synthetic and real features with domain shuffle

model_weights_available.detail: Trained model weights at the same GitHub repository

G1.quote: The development of deep learning-based methods has been hindered by the lack of large-scale datasets with high-quality annotations.

G2.quote: the three-frame setting may not fully generalize across datasets with different motion characteristics, such as acquisition frame rates.

G3.quote: However, these methods operate on individual frames and do not effectively address issues such as motion blur and temporal inconsistency.

G4.quote: addressing key challenges such as motion artifacts, anatomical overlap, and annotation scarcity

G5.quote: By generating large-scale synthetic sequences with realistic motion and anatomical variability, our method circumvents the need for costly and errorprone manual labeling.

other_limitations: Interventional devices (catheters, stents, wires) often misclassified as vessels
Lower temporal consistency than ETRPCA in reader study due to three-frame input
Vessels simulated independently from surrounding tissue
Limited diversity of ~1,500 background images may constrain synthetic data
future_work: Model interventional artifacts in synthesis or add artifact-aware discriminative modules
Integrated simulation of vessels and background tissue prior to projection
Expand background image pool and enrich synthesis process
Extend framework to cerebral and peripheral angiography
